attempt: Access order equals original WRITE order, which GR-VII.2.4.3-2 might not state.
reason: GR-VII.2.4.3-2 says the sequence is specified by predecessor-successor relationships established by WRITE when the file is created or extended; GR-VII.4.7.4-12 adds 'established by the order of execution of WRITE statements'. Same obligation; the original order is the creation-then-extend order.
quoted: the order of sequential access is the order in which the records were originally written

attempt: Successful statuses (04, 05, 07) might still run a USE procedure; the unit forbids it.
reason: GR-VII.4.6.4-5 runs USE procedures 'upon the unsuccessful execution'; L2.1 lists 00/04/05/07 as successful, L2.2-5 as 'With Unsuccessful Completion'. Middle sentence defers to 'rules stated elsewhere', last is a pointer. Nothing left over.
quoted: no such procedure will be executed

attempt: The lead-in closes the set: status expresses exactly one of five conditions.
reason: The sentence ends in a colon and the five numbered rules GR-VII.1.3.5-1..5 each name a condition; closure is the list itself. No tail after the list; no definition or scope of its own.
quoted: I-O status expresses one of the following conditions

attempt: Implementor chooses which value when more than one applies: claimed a new row.
reason: Catalog row 1985-GR-VII.1.3.5-5 already carries this unit's text ('The following is a list of the values placed in the I-O status ... If more than one value applies, the implementor determines which of the applicable values to place in the I-O status.') after its own sentence. The obligation is stated by a named existing row, so the unit is not a new row.
quoted: the implementor determines which of the applicable values to place in the I-O status

attempt: Timing of the status (before the imperative or USE procedure) might be stated by GR-VII.2.5.4-1 or the statement rules.
reason: GR-VII.2.5.4-1 states only that the FILE STATUS item is updated whenever the status is; the before-imperative/USE timing and the two-character entity are not stated by it, and no row carries them. A row stands.
quoted: The I-O status is a two-character conceptual entity

attempt: At end can arise elsewhere than READ, or the READ rule does not state when it arises.
reason: GR-VII.4.4.4-10 states when the at end condition arises on READ (no next logical record / optional input file absent) and what happens. Unit says only that READ can produce it, plus a pointer.
quoted: The at end condition can occur as a result of the execution of a READ statement

attempt: Optionality or placement of the Input-Output Section could differ from the format.
reason: FMT-IV.6.2.3.1 brackets INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION inside ENVIRONMENT DIVISION: optional and located there. Middle sentence is purpose only.
quoted: The Input-Output Section is optional in the Environment Division

attempt: The module-level format could differ from the Environment Division format.
reason: The fenced block INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. FILE-CONTROL. {file-control-entry}... [I-O-CONTROL. [input-output-control-entry]] is identical to the section arm of FMT-IV.6.2.3.1; no extra condition.
quoted: The general format of the Input-Output Section is shown below

attempt: FILE STATUS function adds a duty beyond updating the item.
reason: GR-VII.2.5.4-1: the data item 'is always updated to contain the value of the I-O status'; SR-VII.2.5.3-2 gives its category. Nothing else in the unit.
quoted: specifies a data item which contains the status of an input-output operation

attempt: Unit adds a duty beyond GR-VII.2.6.3-1.
reason: Verbatim first sentence of GR-VII.2.6.3-1; the second sentence (permanence) is not in the unit.
quoted: specifies sequential organization as the logical structure of a file

attempt: Unit adds a padding duty beyond the GR.
reason: Verbatim first sentence of GR-VII.2.7.4-1, which also carries the input/output padding behavior.
quoted: specifies the character which is to be used for block padding

attempt: Unit adds duty beyond the GR.
reason: GR-VII.2.8.4-1 says the clause 'is used to indicate the method of determining the length of a variable length record on the external medium'; same.
quoted: the method of determining the length of a variable length record

attempt: Unit adds duty beyond the GR.
reason: Verbatim first sentence of GR-VII.2.9.3-1, which also gives the count semantics.
quoted: allows the user to specify the number of input-output areas allocated

attempt: Unit states sharing scope the two GRs do not.
reason: GR-VII.2.13.4-1 and -2 each state the shared memory area for SAME AREA and SAME RECORD AREA.
quoted: specifies the memory area which is to be shared by different files

attempt: Immediate adjacency of record descriptions may exceed 'must follow'.
reason: FMT-IV.6.3.2.2.1 writes file-description-entry {record-description-entry}... adjacent; SR-VII.3.2.3-3 requires one or more to follow. 'Defines the structure of data files' is purpose only.
quoted: Record description entries are written immediately following the file description entry

attempt: The Sequential I-O File Section format could be narrower than the global format.
reason: The block FILE SECTION. [file-description-entry {record-description-entry}...]... is the file-description arm of FMT-IV.6.3.2.2.1; the sort-merge and report arms belong to other modules and are not in this unit.
quoted: The general format of the File Section in the Sequential I-O module is shown below

attempt: Claimed the structure sentence is not a rule's.
reason: Its first two sentences (data description entry = level-number, then data-name or FILLER, then clauses) are the data description entry format FMT-VI.5.3.2; hierarchy and clause availability are pointers to IV-14 and VI-20 and per-clause level rules. Not a separate SR row: it restates the format.
quoted: Each data description entry consists of a level-number followed by the data-name or FILLER clause

attempt: File Section initial value might differ from the Nucleus rule.
reason: GR-VI.5.15.6-1 a: 'the initial value of the data items in the File Section is undefined', same words and scope.
quoted: The initial value of a data item in the File Section is undefined

attempt: Claimed BLOCK CONTAINS specifying physical record size is stated by no rule.
reason: GR-VII.3.3.3-3 'the physical record size is specified in terms of the number of character positions' and GR-VII.3.3.3-4 'integer-2 represents the exact size of the physical record' state the same; sibling Function units (3.7.1, 3.8.1) were disposed restates on the same pattern.
quoted: specifies the size of a physical record

attempt: Unit adds duty beyond CODE-SET GR.
reason: GR-VII.3.4.4-1 a/b: the external-media character set is the one named by alphabet-name-1, with conversion; same obligation.
quoted: the character code convention used to represent data on the external media

attempt: Unit states margin or footing meaning the GRs omit.
reason: GR-VII.3.7.4-1 (page depth), -3 (footing line), -4 and -5 (top and bottom margins) cover each clause of the unit.
quoted: specifying the depth of a logical page in terms of number of lines

attempt: Variable-length range or fixed length not stated by GRs.
reason: GR-VII.3.8.4-3 (fixed, integer-1) and -4 (variable, integer-2 minimum, integer-3 maximum) cover it.
quoted: specifies the number of character positions in a fixed length record

attempt: ALL FORMATS label scopes GR1-GR2 in a way not carried.
reason: Unit is only the label ALL FORMATS. GR1 and GR2 are written without format limits, so the label's scope is their default. No sentence.
quoted: ALL FORMATS: (1) If the RECORD clause
